'''Serguei Barannikov''' ({{langx|ru|Сергей Александрович Баранников}}; born April 16, 1972) is a [[mathematician]], known for his works in [[algebraic topology]], [[algebraic geometry]] and [[mathematical physics]].

== Biography ==
Barannikov graduated with honors from [[Moscow State University]] in 1994.

In 1995–1999, Barannikov received his [[Doctor of Philosophy]] degree (Ph.D.) in Mathematics from the [[University of California, Berkeley]]. Simultaneously, he was an invited researcher at [[Institut des Hautes Etudes Scientifiques]] in France.

During 1999–2010, he worked as a researcher at [[Ecole Normale Supérieure]] in Paris. Since 2010, he works as a researcher at [[Paris Diderot University]].

== Scientific work ==
At the age of 20, Barannikov wrote a paper<ref name="FMC">{{Cite journal |last=Barannikov |first=S. |year=1994 |title=Framed Morse complex and its invariants |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/267672645 |journal=Advances in Soviet Mathematics |series=ADVSOV |volume=21 |pages=93–115 |doi=10.1090/advsov/021/03|isbn=9780821802373 |s2cid=125829976 }}</ref> on algebraic topology, in which he introduced the "canonical forms" invariants of filtered complexes, later also called "Barannikov modules".<ref name="BMcomp">{{Cite journal |last1=Le Peutrec |first1=D. |last2=Nier |first2=N. |last3=Viterbo |first3=C. |title=Precise Arrhenius Law for ''p''-forms: The Witten Laplacian and Morse–Barannikov Complex |journal=Annales Henri Poincaré |volume=14 |issue=3 |pages=567–610 |doi=10.1007/s00023-012-0193-9 |year=2013 |bibcode=2013AnHP...14..567L|arxiv=1105.6007 |s2cid=253601705 }}</ref><ref name="modB">{{Cite journal  |arxiv = 1810.03139|title = Barcodes and area-preserving homeomorphisms|last1 = Le Roux|first1 = Frédéric|last2 = Seyfaddini|first2 = Sobhan|last3 = Viterbo|first3 = Claude| journal=Geometry & Topology |year = 2021| volume=25 | issue=6 | pages=2713–2825 | doi=10.2140/gt.2021.25.2713 | s2cid=119133707 }}</ref> Ten years later, these invariants became widely used in applied mathematics in the field of [[Topological data analysis#Early history|topological data analysis]] under the name of [[Persistent homology#Definition|"persistence bar-codes"]] and [[Persistent homology#Definition|"persistence diagrams"]].<ref name="modB" /><ref name="berkeleyClqvm">{{Cite web |url=https://events.berkeley.edu/?event_ID=121726&date=2018-11-29&tab=academic |title=UC Berkeley Mathematics Department Colloquium: Persistent homology and applications from PDE to symplectic topology |publisher=events.berkeley.edu |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210418211352/https://events.berkeley.edu/?event_ID=121726&date=2018-11-29&tab=academic |accessdate=2022-12-16|archive-date=2021-04-18 }}</ref>

Barannikov is known for his work on [[Mirror symmetry (string theory)|mirror symmetry]], [[Morse theory]], and [[Hodge theory]]. In mirror symmetry, he is a co-author of construction of Frobenius manifold, mirror symmetric to genus zero Gromov–Witten invariants.<ref name="cstBK" />

He is one of authors of hypothesis of homological mirror symmetry for Fano manifolds.<ref name="Congr">{{Cite book |last=Seidel |first=P. |chapter=Vanishing Cycles and Mutation |editor1=Casacuberta C. |editor2=Miró-Roig R.M. |editor3=Verdera J. |editor4=Xambó-Descamps S. |title=European Congress of Mathematics |series=Progress in Mathematics |volume=202 |pages=65–85 |year=2001 | isbn= 978-3-0348-8266-8 |publisher= Birkhäuser |arxiv=math/0007115 |doi=10.1007/978-3-0348-8266-8_7 |s2cid=2347878 }}</ref> In the theory of exponential integrals, Barannikov is a co-author of the theorem on the degeneration of analogue of Hodge–de Rham spectral sequence.<ref name="thBK" />

In the theory of noncommutative varieties, Barannikov is the author of the theory of noncommutative Hodge structures.<ref name="nchodge">{{cite book |last1=Katzarkov |first1=L. |last2=Kontsevich |first2=M. |last3=Pantev |date=2008 |chapter= Hodge theoretic aspects of mirror symmetry |title=From Hodge theory to integrability and TQFT tt*-geometry |pages=87–174 |editor1=Ron Y. Donagi |editor2=Katrin Wendland |series= Proceedings of Symposia in Pure Mathematics |volume=78 |arxiv=0806.0107 |bibcode=2008arXiv0806.0107K |isbn=978-0-8218-4430-4 |mr=2483750 |publisher= American Mathematical Society}}</ref>

Barannikov is known for: Barannikov–Morse complexes,<ref name="BMcomp" /> Barannikov modules,<ref name="modB" /> Barannikov–Kontsevich construction,<ref name="cstBK">{{Cite journal |last=Manin |first=Yu.I. |title=Three constructions of Frobenius manifolds: a comparative study |journal=Surveys in Differential Geometry |volume=7 |pages=497–554
 |date= 2002 |arxiv=math/9801006 |doi=10.4310/SDG.2002.v7.n1.a16|s2cid=15448492 }}</ref> and Barannikov–Kontsevich theorem.<ref name="thBK">{{Cite arXiv |eprint = math/0507476 |title = Nonabelian Hodge Theory in Characteristic ''p'' |last1 = Ogus |first1 = Arthur |last2 = Vologodsky |first2 = Vadim | year = 2005 }}</ref>
